reason: Runnable (pure python ints for GF(2^n) + PARI ellcard; <5 CPU-min; metrics are ranks/annihilator dims, not wall time) but as written it does not discriminate. (1) Null arm 'random sets of equal size' is the wrong null: verified in sandbox (n=23, a=1, 300 points) that every point of 2E(F_{2^n}) has Tr(x)=Tr(a) (300/300 vs 171/300 for random E points), and [k]G for G of prime order lies in 2E (cofactor 2 or 4). So x(S_L) has a trivial affine F_2 annihilator Tr(x)+Tr(a), the degree-2 annihilator space contains (Tr(x)+Tr(a))*(affine fn) of dim n+1, and span dim <= n-1: all 'below random' for a reason unrelated to automaticity. Null must be random multiples [k]G of the same subgroup (and for cofactor 4 the second halving condition). (2) F_2-span dimension is vacuous: |S_L|>=2^10 >> n=23,29 so a random set spans everything; only the Tr artefact can move it. (3) Berlekamp-Massey needs a scalar-side scan order and bit/functional choice that the design does not specify; ordering-dependent, not basis-invariant. The faithful automaticity statistic is the F_2 rank of the Hankel/Nerode matrix H[u][v]=bit(x([u*tau^m+v]G)) over prefix u and suffix v of the tau-NAF digit string (automatic or regular => bounded rank/#distinct rows; generic => min(#rows,#cols)). (4) Degree-2 annihilator count is basis-invariant and fine, but at n=23/29 density |S|/2^n is 2^-9..2^-13 near r^{1/2} so toy is in the dense regime where Kohel-Shparlinski type character-sum bounds already predict randomness; and there is no positive control showing the tester can detect planted automatic structure. (5) Scaling: only two n values (23,29) and one ell, so no scaling law; n=131 relevance requires a fixed-ell, varying-n curve and |S|<<sqrt(r). Even a positive result is only a necessary condition: it does not itself give membership testing below log R, so cannot establish B*D^2<<N; it can only reopen the coordinate-side door. Scope of any null: single L (digits < ell), not all regular languages; language classes defined by tau-adic congruences (k in (tau-1)^j Z[tau], etc.) are coset/subgroup conditions and are known structure, not new.
fix: Redesign. Setup: Koblitz K_a over F_{2^n}, n in {23,29,31,41,47,53,59,83} (PARI ellcard for order/cofactor h; G = h*P0 of prime order if available, else just fix G of any large order and record it; pure-python int GF(2^n) arithmetic; Frobenius powers phi^i(G) by repeated squaring so S_L sums are computed as signed sums of conjugates, no tau-NAF conversion needed). Language: tau-NAF strings of length ell (no two adjacent nonzeros), ell in {9,10,11,12,13}, |S_L|~2^(ell+1.4)/... record actual count. Null arms (>=20 draws each, equal size): N1 = [k]G with k uniform in [0,r) (same subgroup, kills Tr(x)=Tr(a) artefact); N2 = signed sums of ell random distinct conjugates phi^{i}(G), i uniform in [0,n) with random positions/signs, no NAF constraint (keeps Frobenius-orbit structure, drops regular-language/ordering structure); N3 = [k]G for k in integer interval [0,|S|) (scalar-side 2-adic automaton, known to be pseudorandom, as sanity). Positive controls: P1 = replace group law by F_2-vector addition: point(u)=sum u_i g_i with random g_i in F_2^n (rank ell, Hankel rank <=ell); P2 = bit b(u)=parity of a fixed subset of digits (Hankel rank 2) to prove the Hankel tester detects automatic/linear-recurrent structure; P3 = degree-2 planted: take x-bits of random subgroup points and append the product of two bits as an extra coordinate, check annihilator found. Metrics (all counted, basis-invariant, no wall time): (M1) dim of F_2-affine span of x(S) minus (n-1) and the number of independent affine annihilators; expected from theory: exactly 1 (Trace) [2 if cofactor 4 gives second condition]; (M2) dim of degree-d annihilator space for d=2 (and d=3 when C(n,<=3) < |S|/2), reported modulo the ideal generated by the already-explained degree-1 annihilators (quotient by (Tr(x)+Tr(a))*Aff) i.e. report excess = dim - (n+1) for d=2; (M3) F_2 Hankel rank of H over prefix/suffix splits m=ell/2 (rows u in NAF prefixes ending in digit 0, columns v), computed for each of the n bit coordinates and for the vertically stacked n-bit matrix (rows = u, cols = (v,coordinate)) to avoid choosing a functional; also number of distinct rows (Nerode class count) and the rank of each mod the all-ones vector. (M4) Frobenius check: fraction of k in S with tau*k in S for which x(tau k)=x(k)^2 (must be 100 percent; confirms the harness, and quantifies the trivially-explained overlap). Decision rule: structure present iff for some (n,ell) the statistic of S_L lies outside the max over 20 N1 draws AND outside N2 AND P-controls are detected; else null = 'indistinguishable from random in same subgroup'. Scaling arm: fix ell in {10,12}, vary n over the list above; report M2 excess and M3 rank deficit (rank vs min(rows,cols)) as function of n and of density log2|S|/n; claim transfer to n=131 only if deficit is non-increasing in n at fixed ell and does not vanish only because density crosses sqrt(r); additionally include one cell with n>=41 where 2^ell < r^{1/2} (n=41..83, ell=12) since n=23/29 with ell=12 is in the dense regime. Also record that the check is necessary-not-sufficient: any positive hit must be followed by a membership-cost test (count of operations to decide R in S_L+S_L from x-bits alone vs log R scalar-side) before it can touch the B*D^2<<N certificate. Budget: <=2^14 points per cell, ~40 cells, GF(2) elimination on packed python ints/numpy; est 3-8 CPU-min total. No msolve/SAT needed.
